notes: Matches the reference: it returns all import statements undeduplicated and moves parent-overrides-child dedup to the per-instance `knownImports.Has` check after expansion, with good plan and apply tests including partial parent/child overrides (the CHANGELOG edit is minor extra scope).

Same approach as the reference: it returns every import statement undeduplicated and moves the parent-overrides-child check to per-instance dedup in expandResourceImports, with solid plan and apply regression tests including a partial parent/child override case; the only extra is a direct CHANGELOG edit.

Fixes the single-module case, but it removes duplicate imports before expansion by statically parsing the `to` expression; when the parent's block is non-static it drops every child import for that resource, and it has no instance-level dedup after expansion, so keyed-module overlaps can let a child block overwrite its parent's.

Tries to decide overrides at config time by statically parsing `to` expressions, which is fragile: dynamic or for_each imports fall back to coarse override, keyed module instances can let the child win, and there is no instance-level dedup after expansion; it also adds unrelated child-sorting and a CHANGELOG edit, though its tests (unit fixture plus for_each and count plan tests) are good.

Uses the same static disjointness heuristic as C1 during traversal and has the same gaps: a non-static parent block suppresses all child imports of that resource, and there is no instance-level check after expansion.

Uses the same config-time static-address heuristic as C3, with the same gaps for dynamic targets and keyed modules and no post-expansion dedup; it adds unneeded child sorting and slices refactors, and its for_each and count tests are duplicated and do not cover module override behavior.

Fixes the reported same-module case, but it still deduplicates across modules at the ConfigResource level, so a parent import of one instance silently drops a child's imports of other instances (the same class of bug as the issue).

Fixes the reported same-module for_each case, but still dedups across modules at ConfigResource granularity, so a parent import of one instance silently drops child-module imports of other instances (the same class of silent drop the issue describes); it has a single for_each test and fails 2/3 hidden tests.

Correct fix using a Dispenser-level `isBlockBrace(string)` helper and cleans up directive() like the reference, but it misses gating the address curly-suffix check on quoting; it adds good dispenser and parser tests, including snippets and nested blocks.

Correct fix using a Dispenser-level isBlockBrace(string) helper; it fixes the quoted '{}' case but misses the quoted address HasSuffix check, and the helper with a string argument is slightly less clean than Token predicates, though its dispenser and parser tests are thorough.

Matches the reference: unquoted-brace helper methods are used everywhere, including the address-suffix check and the `{}` branch, and docs are updated; it adds thorough dispenser, parser and snippet tests plus an integration adapt test that is somewhat beyond the minimum.

Complete match to the reference including doc comments, the address-suffix check and the '{}' fix; tests are very thorough (dispenser, parser, snippets, imported snippets), and the added caddyfile_adapt integration test is useful but slightly broadens scope.

Core fix is correct, but it leaves the address HasSuffix check and the `{}` branch ungated on quoting and keeps a now-redundant wasQuoted check in directive(); tests are strong, including imported block contents and heredoc/backtick cases.

The core fix is correct and the helpers are clean, but it leaves a redundant wasQuoted check after isOpenCurlyBrace and does not fix the quoted '{}' branch or the quoted address-suffix check; its tests cover backticks, heredocs and import-with-block.

Functionally equivalent to the reference, covering the address suffix, the `{}` gating and directive() cleanup; tests are concise table entries (including heredoc and nested cases) but only check segment counts, and the RemainingArgs docs are not updated.

Nearly identical to the reference: it adds Token helper methods, replaces every structural brace check (including the quoted address-suffix and quoted '{}' fixes), and adds solid table cases; the only gap is that the RemainingArgs doc comments were not updated.
